candidates.name: malignant pleural mesothelioma
support_spans: multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with pleural thickenings and effusion, along with the pathological findings of epithelioid solid formations, suggests malignant pleural mesothelioma.

candidates.name: tongue metastasis of malignant mesothelioma
support_spans: Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue.
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
candidates.why: The appearance of a nodular growth on the tongue, with pathological findings consistent with mesothelial origin, suggests a metastasis of malignant mesothelioma.

candidates.name: malignant pleural mesothelioma
support_spans: homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
candidates.why: The homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene is a common genetic alteration in malignant pleural mesothelioma, suggesting a mechanism of tumorigenesis.

candidates.name: desmoplastic malignant mesothelioma
support_spans: Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
candidates.why: The presence of epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures is consistent with desmoplastic malignant mesothelioma, a subtype of mesothelioma with a distinct mechanism of tumorigenesis.
